notes:
PASS on the fake backend only; evidence is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. This package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null); RosDriver refuses every hardware backend without a human hardware review, and no ROS graph, infra_sensor_urg node, LiDAR, Unity simulator or hardware run was used or claimed.

The selected device is the concrete ROS 2 infra_sensor_urg node lidar_subscriber, not the repository's Unity/Hakoniwa demo as a whole. It publishes geometry_msgs/msg/Twist on the absolute /TB3RoboAvatar_cmd_pos topic (lidar_subscriber.py:5,78; README.md:451-465). The package is a configuration-only ROS 2 RosDriver over rosbridge; it declares no Python native class and no native.py. It binds one fresh cap.sensing.read.v1 topic subscription and projects the Twist into the class's open values object: linear x,y,z -> metres, angular x,y,z -> roll,pitch,yaw radians. geometry_msgs/Twist has no header, so sampled_at is the driver's local receive stamp, not the publisher's sample time. Unknown channel names in the optional fields array are ignored; the class example input therefore completes with an empty values object.

The node's LaserScan and Imu input topics (/LiDARSensor2D_scan and /TB3RoboModel_imu with act_mode=sim; /scan and /tb3_imu otherwise) are not bound. The driver observes the node's published estimate and cannot step the estimator. act_mode is a startup ROS 2 parameter read once in the constructor (lidar_subscriber.py:66-73); set_scan_mode is reached only through the interactive PyQt keyboard monitor (lidar_subscriber.py:144-157,173-176), and the pinned node creates no ROS service, action or runtime-parameter endpoint for it. The registry also lists cap.device.configure.v1, but no source-backed runtime configure endpoint exists at this pin, so this package binds only the read class, declares no numeric input or Limit, and keeps risk at the card floor R1. The card's HakoPduServer/websocket and estimator-class hints were not selected: the webserver is a Hakoniwa PDU bridge requiring hakopy/hako_pdu and a running asset, and the estimator class is wrapped by the selected ROS 2 node.

The card's upstream-sim preference was not usable here: the Unity/Hakoniwa simulator and hako runtime are outside the pinned clone or unavailable, and the repository's real/test test exercises the Hako PDU estimator, not the selected ROS 2 publication. The fake is a ROS-free event-driven canned transcript (F0, engine 'canned:ROS 2 /TB3RoboAvatar_cmd_pos transcript...') that answers only the declared subscription with placeholder Twist messages; it runs no estimator, LiDAR filter, PyQt plotter, ROS graph or physics. All its values and negative switches are placeholders, and its pose does not establish position accuracy.

Safety: the node is a passive publisher. The package declares no actuation, native stop, reset or safe-state action. The stock e-stop reports estop 'software_only' with latched true and safe_state_achieved true because there is no actuating capability; that is the SDK's read-only latch behavior, not a native or physical stop claim. A catalogue-confirmed read remains available during the latch.

The fake covers a silent topic, an unrelated event id, a rejected subscription, malformed missing/string Twist fields and a non-object sample; test_driver.py has the stock gate plus ten repository cases. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning remains; the only warning is G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE, expected because a read-only sensor declares no numeric actuation limit. The clone was left unmodified (G1 passed). No network, pip install, upstream execution or hardware was used. No preflight section for this exact package and pin was present in the two named PREFLIGHT.md files.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the bound /TB3RoboAvatar_cmd_pos subscription (endpoint and type at lidar_subscriber.py:5, 78), the output mapping and finite checks, all 15 facts, the fake, the read-only software latch and the card's unselected hints against infra_sensor_urg, pos_estimator.py, lidar_params.py, the tg15 node, tb3_controller.cpp and the README at the pin. The binding is right, but the read was misdescribed: x and y are 0.0, not an estimate, while the estimator collects its 50 environment scans and, after the message that completes the scan, until an operator enters 's' at the node's terminal (lidar_subscriber.py:121-133, pos_estimator.py:65, 227-252), whereas a gap said the keyboard monitor was needed 'to leave scan mode'; three facts said more than their lines (the subscriptions are on 83-92, not 66-73; 'from the estimator' and 'from the IMU Euler angles' were off 135-142, which also hid the 0.0 branch; the lidar_params import), and the README fact hid that its prose names RobotAvator_cmd_pos. Undisclosed: the clone's infra_sensor_tg15 node publishes on the same topic, and tb3_controller_node, which the README runs with act_mode:=real against a TurtleBot3, takes it as its position input. The reviewer changed driver.py (docstring; five facts corrected, the lidar_params-import fact replaced and thirteen added; three gaps added and the scan-mode gap rewritten; the read description now says when x and y are 0.0), fake.py (a non-finite pitch switch), test_driver.py (a case that a NaN angle never becomes a value) and facts.md, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate and collect.py --strict pass (only G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE) with the digest unchanged (sha256:9824255f1861cff87122d4c2af43e78e35d22377166a494ca7689580adee7b4f); the author's notes count ten repository cases, now eleven. The card needs the owner's publication decision (publish_review required; licence not stated (NOASSERTION)); the package may not be published or merged into a published tree before it. For the human reviewer: Read-only: the package only subscribes to /TB3RoboAvatar_cmd_pos and never publishes. That topic is also the position input of the clone's tb3_controller_node, which in act_mode real drives a real TurtleBot3 on /tb3_cmd_vel and uses linear.x to decide where to stop for a virtual signal; the README's documented deployment is act_mode real with a real URG LiDAR, while the package keeps the card's simulated mode. x = y = 0.0 means no estimate until an operator types 's' at the node's terminal; a consumer must not read it as a robot at the sensor origin. Licence: the infra_sensor_urg manifest says TOPPERS, the card NOASSERTION; publish_review required.
